public_rationale: Marcus's qualified observation has substantial support: reporting documents human assistance with We Robot interactions, and a Tesla engineer confirmed teleoperation in the November hand demonstration. However, Tesla also described a separate October demonstration as autonomous. The records do not identify which demonstrations Marcus meant or establish the division of practical judgment across them. Restricting the claim to We Robot would add a scope he did not supply; treating every autonomous movement as a refutation would also overstate the evidence. The full claim remains unresolved.
limitations: “Apparently” is preserved as a qualification, not converted into certainty.
The time window is an explicit evaluator choice.
Company autonomy statements are disclosures, not independent verification.
We Robot evidence relies on contemporaneous reporting because detailed primary operational records were not obtained.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: In recent Optimus demonstrations, all or most of the required commonsense was apparently supplied by human teleoperators.

statement.excerpt: In Elon Musk’s recent Optimus demonstrations, all or most of the commonsense required was apparently outsourced to human teleoperators.
statement.document_title: AI still lacks “common” sense, 70 years later

from_speaker: all or most of the commonsense required
our_interpretation: Assess the qualified attribution expressed by “apparently,” rather than treating the sentence as a categorical assertion that every action was remotely controlled.
Read “commonsense required” as the practical judgment needed to perform the demonstrated tasks. This is an evaluator interpretation, not a measure Marcus supplied.
Use 2024-10-01 through 2025-01-04 as a provisional window for “recent” before the January 5 post. Marcus supplied no exact boundary or list of demonstrations.
Consider We Robot and other demonstrations within that window; do not silently restrict the claim to We Robot.

Do not equate the share of commonsense with the share of motor commands, robots, demonstrations, or elapsed time. Autonomous movement alone neither establishes nor disproves autonomous practical judgment.
“Apparently” qualifies confidence; it is not an antecedent that must occur.
criteria.support_condition: Credible evidence about the demonstrations Marcus meant provides a reasonable basis for attributing all or most of their required practical judgment to human teleoperators, while allowing some autonomous capabilities.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Credible evidence about those same demonstrations shows that autonomous systems supplied most of the required practical judgment, undermining the qualified attribution to human teleoperators. Evidence of some autonomous functions alone is insufficient.
